newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on fears of intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on fears of intervention.

text.p: The won closed lower on Tuesday on a remark by a central Bank of Korea official that the bank was considering buying dollars because it wanted the dollar to strengthen against the local currency, dealers said.
The bank official, who asked not to be identified, said it would be desirable for the won to move in line with other Asian currencies against the dollar on world markets.
"Abundant dollar liquidity has prevented the dollar from strengthening. We are considering soaking up dollars in the market, if the dollar cannot rebound by itself," he said.
The won ended at 890.30 against Monday's close of 888.90.
"The remark fuelled dollar-buying interest as there had been intervention fears," said a local bank dealer.
It is unusual for central bank officials to publicly discuss the possibility of intervening.
After opening at the high of 888.80, the won fell to the day's low of 890.60 on some short-covering but further falls were limited on dollar profit-taking, dealers said.
"The dollar is unlikely to trade below the 890 won level," said a foreign bank dealer.
Wednesday's mid-rate would be pegged at 890.00 against 888.90 today. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
